## Course Philosophy

This course is structured around a single inversion: **start with the business problem, then introduce the data method** — never the other way around. Every week begins with a decision that needs to be made, and ends with a deliverable that makes that decision.

> "You have 3 models. Which one do you deploy, and why — from a business perspective?" — the kind of question that runs through every module.

## Course Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Foundations | 1–2 | Decision mindset, data quality, problem framing |
| 2 — Analytics core | 3–5 | Experimentation, storytelling, customer intelligence |
| 3 — Revenue & product | 6–9 | Product, recommenders, pricing, fraud |
| 4 — Advanced & ethics | 10–11 | Forecasting, GDPR, EU AI Act |
| 5 — Capstone | 12–14 | Team AI product + investor pitch |

## Assessment Philosophy

### What gets graded
Every major deliverable in this course asks for a **recommendation**, not just an analysis. A segmentation notebook without a marketing strategy gets partial credit. A fraud threshold without a business justification gets partial credit. A pitch with great model accuracy but no ROI argument fails the pitch component.

### Grading Breakdown
| Type | Weight |
|---|---|
| Weekly deliverables (memos, notebooks, briefs) | 40% |
| Midterm case exam (week 7) | 15% |
| Participation (debates, presentations) | 15% |
| Capstone | 30% |

## Tools & Stack

| Category | Tools |
|---|---|
| Data wrangling | `pandas`, `numpy` |
| Visualisation | `matplotlib`, `seaborn`, `plotly` |
| Statistics & experiments | `scipy.stats`, `pingouin` |
| Machine learning | `scikit-learn` |
| Forecasting | `Prophet`, `statsmodels` |
| Notebooks | Jupyter |
| Version control | GitHub (mandatory from week 2) |

## Reading

- *Thinking Fast and Slow* — Kahneman
- *Naked Statistics* — Wheelan
- *Storytelling with Data* — Knaflic
- *The Elements of Statistical Learning* — Hastie et al.
- EU AI Act full text
- GDPR Articles 5, 6, 13, 17, 22
